operation_tail.detail: The UK-and-nations fixed coverage file is documented as 495 data rows and 28 KB; it is a national summary product, not the postcode join source.
The UK-and-nations file distinguishes All, Residential and Commercial premise types; denominators are not mixed.
The national file distinguishes Total, Urban and Rural categories; rurality aggregates are not assigned to parcel rows.
Premise Base, Unclassified, threshold bands, Full Fibre and Gigabit capable are coverage categories and are not represented as measured parcel speed.
The national summary contains both percentage and count fields; percentages are not reverse-engineered into postcode premise counts.
The documented date field is Jan-26 and remains bound to the January 2026 snapshot.
The local-authority full-fibre take-up file is documented as 361 rows and 11 KB; it is not a postcode-level coverage source.
Take-up uses active residential or business full-fibre lines providing an active broadband service, not availability predictions.
One take-up field uses all premises with full-fibre coverage as its denominator and remains separate from coverage availability.
A second take-up field uses all premises in the local authority as its denominator; the two percentages are not interchanged.
Ofcom notes that take-up as a share of coverage can fall when coverage grows faster even while active connections increase.
Local-authority all-premises and residential coverage files each contain 361 rows and remain distinct.
Westminster constituency all-premises and residential coverage files each contain 650 rows and remain distinct.
Devolved constituency all-premises and residential coverage files each contain 131 rows and remain distinct.
Output-area files contain 238,878 all-premises rows and 238,850 residential rows; differing totals are preserved.
Output areas use the 2021 census for England, Northern Ireland and Wales and the 2022 census for Scotland; geography vintages are not conflated.
Ofcom states fields may appear in a different order; parsing must use header names rather than fixed column positions.
The postcode-area field is preserved separately from postcode and postcode_space to validate the expected inner-file area.
All Premises count is absent from postcode files, preventing unsupported premise-count derivation at postcode level.
All Matched Premises count is absent from postcode files; matched denominators cannot be reconstructed from postcode percentages alone.
Documented number-of-premises coverage fields are excluded from postcode files and are not synthesized.
A premise is matched only when linked to at least one fixed-provider record with a non-zero predicted download speed.
Unmatched premises are classified as unclassified rather than assigned a zero or inferred coverage result.
Unable-to-receive 2, 5, 10 or 30 Mbit/s percentages use matched premises as the denominator.
The fixed-or-FWA decent-broadband field explicitly includes unmatched records and zero predicted speeds, so it is not interchangeable with matched-only fields.
The NGA definition covers active fixed-line connections except ADSL and includes full fibre, HFC, VDSL and G.Fast.
The 0 to 2 Mbit/s maximum-download band is preserved as a defined interval rather than a point estimate.
The 2 to 5 and 5 to 10 Mbit/s bands remain separate and are not collapsed into a single inferred speed.
The 10 to 30, 30 to 300 and at-least-300 Mbit/s bands remain distinct availability categories.
Thirty official table, denominator, topology and parser controls were published line by line; no live owner or active PENDING was found and no coverage candidate was promoted without exact r2 bytes.
